svg.title: Nine ways information crosses the wall
svg.desc: A padlocked dashed wall divides a TRAIN block from the test side, crossed by nine red arrows whose thickness is proportional to the measured inflation each kind of leakage produces, from 33.50 points for feature selection on all labels down to 2.28 for duplicate rows, with a green Pipeline box below noted as blocking five of the nine by construction and a shuffled-label test whose 0.72 bar is crossed out against the 0.50 it should have produced.
svg.text: Nine ways information crosses the wall
TEST - what the model must not see
+26.19 a column that only exists for churners
+15.24 AUC SMOTE applied before the split
+15.30 AUC a shuffled split on a time series
+13.32 target encoding on the full set
+6.67 scaler fitted on all data (n=60, p=200)
the same scaler leak at n=5,000 is +0.00. The
SIZE depends on what leaked and how much data
you have - the ORDER does not.
this blocks five of the nine by construction
shuffle y and the AUC must land on 0.50
...and the leaks a test cannot catch? -> the checklist
